title: Nature Walk — Signs of Spring
strapline: Out looking for buds, blossom and the first insects — proof that the season really is turning.
intent: Children observe seasonal growth in their own local environment.
Children connect what they have grown indoors to what is happening outside.
Collecting and describing treasures builds vocabulary and close observation.
Walking the same route repeatedly makes change visible in a way one walk cannot.
The local patch becomes somewhere children know well and care about.
implementation: Take children outside to look for buds, flowers, insects or changing trees.
Walk the same short route several times across the half-term so change is noticeable.
Collect natural objects — leaves, petals, twigs — where it is safe and responsible to do so.
Introduce descriptive language as you go: bud, blossom, sprout, shoot, bare, green.
Let children set the pace and stop where they want to stop.
Encourage children to share what they notice with each other, not only with you.
Bring the treasures back to a nature table and revisit them indoors.
key_questions: What can you see today that was not here last time?
What do you think this bud will turn into?
How does this leaf feel? What could we compare it to?
Where is the best place to look for something growing?
What do you think we will find on our next walk?

impact.text: Children talk about what they see and find on local walks and collect treasures.
Children notice seasons changing and what that means.
Children know their local patch as a learner.
Children take up rich descriptive vocabulary and use it back.
Children ask real questions about growth and change and expect real answers.
Children negotiate space and uneven ground with growing confidence.

enhancements: A nature table restocked after every walk, with magnifiers alongside.
A "same tree" photo series taken from an identical spot each visit.
A collection of rubbings and prints made from the leaves and bark collected.
A sound map — stand still, close eyes, draw what you can hear.
A spring checklist the children design and tick off as they find each sign.
A link back to the planting activity — what is growing outside, and what is growing on our windowsill?

playing_exploring: Children explore freely outdoors and follow whatever catches their eye.
active_learning: Children look carefully and return to the same spots to check for change.
They sustain attention across a walk and back at the nature table.
creating_thinking: Children predict what a bud will become and check on the next walk.
They connect indoor growing to outdoor growing and see the same process.
